solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Fish left in straw hats

indicators.note: in says the letter for left is placed inside the word for the hats

parts.note: boaters are flat-topped straw hats

explanation.surface: Someone has left fish lying inside straw hats.
explanation.definitionFit: Bloaters are herrings that have been salted and smoked whole, a kind of cured fish.

clue.text: Leave? Absolutely, but not the end

indicators.note: not the end says the final letter of the word for absolutely is dropped

parts.note: quite can mean absolutely, as in 'quite right'

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether to leave and is told yes, just not at the finish.
explanation.definitionFit: To quit a place or job is to leave it; the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Les and Rod punished, getting flogged again

indicators.note: punished suggests the two names are knocked about, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Two men named Les and Rod were punished and then whipped a second time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flogged' looks like a beating to go with 'punished', but here it is the slang sense of sold.
explanation.definitionFit: To flog is informal British for to sell, so goods flogged again have been sold a second time.

clue.text: Hunter's assistant to reverse into gee-gee

indicators.note: into says the word for reversing an action goes inside the horse's letters

parts.note: gee-gee is a childish word for a horse, written GG
to undo something is to reverse what was done

explanation.surface: A hunter's helper is told to back a horse into position.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reverse' suggests turning letters backwards, but it is a synonym: to reverse an action is to undo it.
explanation.definitionFit: A gundog is trained to help a shooter by finding and retrieving game, the hunter's helper.

clue.text: Old pack leader's forehead now large

parts.note: the brow is the forehead
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: An elderly pack leader's forehead has grown large.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Brownies, the junior branch of the Girl Guides, a pack's adult leader was traditionally called Brown Owl.
explanation.definitionFit: The title was given to whoever led a Brownie pack, a usage now largely dropped, hence old.

clue.text: Do as told and honour Yankee

parts.note: the OBE, Order of the British Empire, is a British honour
Yankee is Y in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An American is told to comply and to show respect.
explanation.definitionFit: To obey is to carry out instructions, doing what one is told.

clue.text: Copper outside, look, to employ a bungling inspector

indicators.note: outside says the chemical symbol for copper goes round the other pieces

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
lo is an old word meaning look
to employ something is to use it

explanation.surface: A policeman, standing outside, decides to hire a hopeless detective.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' invites a policeman, fitting the inspector, but it is the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Inspector Clouseau is the clumsy French detective of the Pink Panther films.

clue.text: Polish face of yellow gemstone

parts.note: to polish something is to rub it

indicators.note: the face of a word is its front, so its first letter is taken

explanation.surface: Someone is told to polish the surface of a yellow jewel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' is the verb, not the nationality, despite its capital.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruby is a precious red stone, a variety of corundum.

clue.text: Some withdrawing support sacked old world leader

indicators.note: withdrawing says the hidden letters are read backwards
Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some backers are pulling out after a former head of state was sacked.
explanation.definitionFit: Fidel Castro led Cuba for about half a century, a former head of state on the world stage.

clue.text: Drab and dull old woman depresses you, first of all

indicators.note: first of all says the opening letter of each of the five words is taken

explanation.surface: A dreary old woman gets you down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drab and dull' looks like a paired definition, but only 'Drab' defines; 'dull' starts the initial letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Dowdy describes something unfashionable and dull in appearance, which is what drab means.

clue.text: A sign of pride?

parts.note: a group of lions is a pride, and the zodiac sign of the lion is this one

explanation.surface: Something that shows a person is proud.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a display of self-respect; the trick is 'pride' as a group of lions.
explanation.definitionFit: The zodiac sign represented by a lion, the animal that lives in prides.

clue.text: FBI agent backed objective to protect

indicators.note: backed says the word for the agent is turned back to front

parts.note: a fed is American slang for an FBI agent
an end is an aim or objective

explanation.surface: An FBI agent supported a goal of keeping someone safe.
explanation.definitionFit: To defend is to guard or shield from attack, the same as to protect.

clue.text: Queen with a fur that can be removed

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen
sable is the prized fur of a small mammal

explanation.surface: A queen wears a fur she can take off.
explanation.definitionFit: Something erasable can be rubbed out or deleted, so it is able to be removed.

clue.text: Classes rise to welcome king and son

indicators.note: to welcome is to take in, so the king's letter goes inside the phrase for rising

parts.note: to rise is to go up
R, for Rex, is the abbreviation for king
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: Pupils stand up to greet a king and his son.
explanation.definitionFit: Classes are categories or sets, as are groups.

clue.text: Nothing American about unusual Azeri restaurant

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the slang for nothing is read backwards

parts.note: zip is American slang for nothing

indicators.note: unusual says the letters of the following word are put in an odd order

explanation.surface: There is nothing American about a strange restaurant from Azerbaijan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nothing American' reads as one unit, the US slang for nothing, and 'about' turns it round; the surface pretends the restaurant is simply not American.
explanation.definitionFit: A pizzeria is an eatery that specialises in pizza.

clue.text: Trembling like a fish

parts.note: as can mean like, as in 'as good as new'
a hake is a fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: Someone is quivering like a fish on a line.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashake is a literary adjective meaning shaking, so trembling in the same sense.

clue.text: Red jeep city's regularly used for drives out

indicators.note: regularly used says every second letter of these words is taken

explanation.surface: A red jeep is often seen being driven about town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drives' suggests motoring with the jeep, but it is the expelling sense.
explanation.definitionFit: To eject someone is to force them out, which is to drive them out.

clue.text: Insect that buzzes around girl in the country

indicators.note: around says the insect's letters surround the girl's name

parts.note: a bee is an insect that buzzes
Liz is a girl's name, short for Elizabeth

explanation.surface: A bee hums around a girl somewhere abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Belize is a nation in Central America, on the Caribbean coast.

clue.text: Bad vibe about second supporting film

indicators.note: about says the rearranged letters go round the short word for a second
bad signals the letters of the next word are spoiled and rearranged

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a second

explanation.surface: A low-quality film gives off a bad feeling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bad' turns VIBE into BVIE, which goes about MO.
explanation.definitionFit: A B-movie was the cheap second feature shown in support of the main film.

clue.text: Fix something to eat with bread

definitions.meaning: a fix is a tight spot or predicament
a fruit preserve spread on bread

explanation.surface: A recipe for something to put on toast.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in a jam means being in a fix, and jam is also the fruit spread for bread.

clue.text: Second rate garden tool that will slow you down

parts.note: B grade is second rate
a rake is a toothed garden tool

explanation.surface: A poor-quality garden tool is hard work and holds you up.
explanation.definitionFit: A brake is the device on a vehicle used to reduce its speed.

clue.text: Little sign one's expecting to make an impact

definitions.meaning: the swelling of a pregnant woman's belly

explanation.surface: An expectant mother's first sign is about to make itself felt.
explanation.definitionFit: A pregnant woman's rounded belly is called her bump, and to bump is to collide.

clue.text: Warning sign about endless trouble for well owners?

indicators.note: about says the omen's letters go round the shortened word for trouble

parts.note: an omen is a warning sign

indicators.note: endless says the last letter of the word for trouble is dropped

parts.note: ill means trouble or harm

explanation.surface: A bad omen warns of trouble for people who own wells.
explanation.walkthrough: 'well owners' suggests water wells; the question mark flags oil wells.
explanation.definitionFit: Oilmen run oil businesses, and oil comes from wells, so they own wells in a playful sense.

clue.text: Heard couple's cat

indicators.note: heard says the word is taken by how it sounds, not how it is spelt

parts.note: couple's read as couples, the verb, which means links

explanation.surface: Someone has heard about a couple's pet cat.
explanation.definitionFit: The lynx is a wild member of the cat family with tufted ears.

clue.text: This boy has turned a shade of green

indicators.note: has turned says the colour's letters are read in the other direction

parts.note: lime is a bright shade of green

explanation.surface: A lad has gone green, perhaps from sickness.
explanation.definitionFit: Emil is a boy's given name, as in the children's book Emil and the Detectives.

clue.text: I rate inn poorly lots of years

indicators.note: poorly suggests the letters are badly arranged and need reordering

explanation.surface: Someone judges an inn as bad and has done for many years.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lots' here means batches: each triennium is a lot of three years.
explanation.definitionFit: A triennium is a three-year period, so the plural names groups of years.
